description: A medieval kingdom of feuding noble houses where magic is real but rare: hedge-witches brew remedies and court mages bend fire, at great personal cost. There are guilds, tournaments and monster-haunted forests. Also, magic does not exist and only charlatans claim it, yet wizards openly cast fireballs in the streets. I start as a squire with no lord.

core.name: The Shattered Crown
core.tagline: Magic is spoken of in whispers — but the fire in the street is always burning.
core.premise: A kingdom of feuding noble houses where magic is both celebrated and feared, with competing truths: some believe in rare, ancient magic, others deny it entirely, yet both sides live with fire, blood, and the constant threat of supernatural violence.
core.tone: Dense, grounded, tense — a world where truth is fragile, and
core.intro: You stand at the edge of a muddy lane in the shadow of a collapsed gate, your tunic torn, your belt unfastened. No lord has claimed you. No house has offered you protection. The wind carries the smell of charred stone and wet grass — and somewhere, a fireball flares in the square, not from a mage, but from a smith’s forge. You don’t know if that was magic or just a trick of the wind. You don’t know if you’re supposed to believe it. But you do know: the market stalls are open,
contradictions_resolved: The description claims both that magic exists and that it doesn’t — this is resolved by asserting that magic *is* real but *rare and deeply controversial*, with
physics: Normal gravity and mechanics apply. Objects fall, people walk, fire burns.
Magic, when it occurs, behaves like a physical force: it requires energy, causes observable damage, and has limited range. Fireballs cast by wizards are not eth
impossible: True, permanent, unexplained magic (e.g. teleportation without cost, healing of
common_knowledge: People know fire can be cast — even if they don’t know how.
People know that some say magic is real, others say it’s fraud. Both sides claim to have seen fireballs or healings.
People know that the forests beyond the western wall are haunted — not by ghosts, but by things that move in the dark and do not speak.

magic.summary: Magic is real but rare, inconsistent, and often dangerous. It appears in specific forms: fire manipulation by court mages, healing or tinctures by hedge-witches. Every use costs the caster — pain, illness, or even death. No one knows where,

technology.summary: Stone buildings, wooden wheels, hand-crafted tools. No iron armor, no steam. Some towns have windmills and bell towers, but no machines. Communication is by word, horn, or rider. Maps are hand-drawn and rarely accurate.

facts.content: A fireball was seen in the market yesterday, but no one saw the caster. The fire didn’t burn down the shop — it fizzled out mid-air. People still don’t know who did it.
